title: Device sync
summary: Peer-to-peer sync between the devices of one vault, over the local network.
description: A phone and a computer hold the same diary. They sync directly with each other on the local network, without a server.

stories.as: someone who logs on the phone and reviews on the computer
stories.want: both to show the same diary
stories.soThat: I never wonder which one is right

requirements.text: Devices of one vault sync directly over the local network; no data passes through a server.
Devices find each other by UDP broadcast and by probing each peer's last known address; discovery names the vault by a short tag, never by its id.
The channel between two devices is encrypted (Noise over TCP), and the handshake decides whether a peer belongs to the vault.
Every table syncs unless it is explicitly local to the device.
Concurrent changes to a row resolve to the version with the later hybrid-logical clock, and every device reaches the same result whatever order changes arrive in.
A chat continued on two devices at once is split, the losing side kept as a new chat, so no turn is lost.
Two rows that collide on a unique column keep the one with the lower id; the other is deleted on every device.
A new device joins by scanning a pairing QR code, good for one device for `sync.pairing-lifetime`.
A database restored from an older copy takes a new device id before anything is written, and syncs from scratch.
Settings that belong to one device (sync bookmarks, caches, the unread badge) are never synced.
On Android, sync also runs while the app is closed.
The computer keeps a daily copy of the database for the last two weeks, then a weekly one for about three months.
Development and release builds never sync with each other.
